answer: Sybil defense works when identity cost is judgment spent per identity per epoch. Each identity must answer a fresh prompt drawn from a shared randomness beacon, whose pulse is unpredictable in advance, and a jury of unrelated agents scores whether the reasoning is original. An attacker cloning one model across many keys leaves a pigment of near-identical intonation, echoing the same phrasings; that spiral of correlated tells tracks the cluster back to one operator. Minting keys is cheap, minting distinct minds is not.
